chunks: And the Commander of the Faithful عليه السلام said:

There is no speaking while the Imam is delivering the sermon, and no turning around except as is permissible in salat (prayer). The jumu‘ah prayer was only made two rak‘ahs because of the two sermons; they were made in place of the last two rak‘ahs, so it is salat (prayer) until the Imam descends.

key_terms.الْإِمَامُ: the prayer leader delivering the sermon and leading the congregation
key_terms.الْتِفَاتَ: turning around or diverting one’s attention
key_terms.الْخُطْبَتَيْنِ: the two sermons that precede the jumu‘ah prayer

ai.seo_question: Why is speaking forbidden during the jumu‘ah sermon, and how are the two sermons related to the prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith states the ruling of maintaining the decorum of salat (prayer) while the Imam is delivering the jumu‘ah sermon. It explains that the two sermons take the place of the final two rak‘ahs, so the state of prayer-related attentiveness continues until the Imam descends.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1230 - The Commander of the Faithful Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) said:

"There is to be no speaking while the Imam is delivering the sermon, and no turning around except as is permissible during prayer. The Jumu’ah prayer was made two rak'ahs because of the two sermons, which have taken the place of the last two rak'ahs. Therefore, it remains as part of the prayer until the Imam descends (finishes the sermon)."
